ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows a rectangular silicon bar labeled “n-Si”, with both ends connected by wires to the DC power supply above, and the power supply is labeled 10 V; below the silicon bar, a dashed double arrow marks the end-to-end length as 1 cm. Then reason: the average electron drift velocity is given by v_d = μ_n E. The electric field E = V/L = 10 V / 1 cm = 10 V/cm. Given μ_n = 1000 cm^2/(V·s), therefore v_d = 1000 × 10 = 10^4 cm/s. The time required to pass through the length 1 cm is t = L/v_d = 1 cm / 10^4 cm/s = 10^-4 s. Converted to microseconds: 10^-4 s = 100 μs.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a 10 V dc supply is wired across the ends of a rectangular n-Si bar, with the end-to-end bar length marked 1 cm. From the text take N_D = 10^16 cm^-3 and μ_n = 1000 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. Let the cross-sectional area be A. With n ≈ N_D and E = V/L, the current is I = q n μ_n (V/L) A. The total electron charge contained in the bar is Q = q n A L. The average time for the population of electrons to be swept through the bar is t = Q/I = L^2/(μ_n V). Substitute L = 1 cm, μ_n = 1000 cm^2/V·s, V = 10 V to get t = 1/(1000×10) s = 10^-4 s = 100 μs.
